rationale: Tenth investigation, taking up the second entry point that the previous Candidate recorded: the startup reconstruction path. The first artifact of c-snapshot-install-commit-context settled the runtime install path, where the published commit index stays below the applied snapshot index until a leader advertises a value; this Candidate states the same publishing duty for the recovery path, where the node rebuilds its own state from a stored snapshot before any leader contacts it. The map carries the fact f-commit-index, its producer and consumers, and the recovery behaviour b-newraft-recovery, which the previous question already cited as the second entry point; this product adds the omitted producer side of that path as its own obligation, with a binding for the restoreSnapshot declaration because a check cannot declare a binding on its own.

candidate.rationale: New Candidate for the recovery entry point of the commit-context duty. It binds the publishing duty to restoreSnapshot, which publishes the applied and snapshot indexes and the configurations from the stored snapshot but never writes the commit index.

question.question: When a node reconstructs its state at startup from a snapshot it stores at index J, does the commit context it publishes - Raft.CommitIndex(), documented as the committed index and as the basis for the read-index optimisation - identify a commit point at least J, or does the node hold applied state at J, and report the restored snapshot itself, while publishing a lower commit index?
question.importance: This is the state a node is in before any leader contacts it, and on the recovery path it is not a transient window: the node reports commit index zero while Stats reports the same node's restored snapshot index and applied index as J, so any client or monitor that relates the commit point to the applied point sees an inconsistency for as long as the node is isolated. The read-index optimisation the accessor is documented to support cannot be derived from a node that reports the committed point below the state it has itself restored, and the snapshot content is by construction committed state: this node produced it after committing and applying those entries.
participants: the node before the restart, as the producer of the stored snapshot
the same node after the restart, as the publisher of the commit context
a client reading the restarted node's commit index or Stats
objects: raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot set by restoreSnapshot
the commit_index, applied_index and last_snapshot_index entries of Raft.Stats
contexts: a node constructed over stores that already hold a snapshot and its log
the prefix after construction and before any election or leader contact
event_paths: producing path: the node commits and applies entries, Snapshot persists the FSM at the applied index and compacts the log, and the node reports commit, applied and last as that index
restart path: the same stores are handed to NewRaft, the snapshot is restored through the FSM, and lastApplied, lastSnapshot, committed configuration and latest configuration are published from it
observation path: the restarted node's commit index, applied index, last index, restored snapshot index and state are read through the public accessors

supporting_behavior_ids.b-newraft-recovery: the recovery behaviour that reconstructs the node's state from the log and the snapshot store at construction; it publishes the applied and snapshot indexes from the stored snapshot but not the commit index, which is the omission the question asks about
supporting_behavior_ids.b-install-snapshot: the runtime sibling of the same omission, already confirmed for the install path, which is why the recovery path is treated as a separate entry point rather than as the same prefix

counterevidence: The map records the follower's commit index as min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex), which describes the append path only and can be read as defining the published value as the last advertised commit index.
No source in the captured module states that the commit index must be advanced when a snapshot is restored at startup.
The restarted node's FSM has the state either way, so an application that reads its own FSM rather than the published index is unaffected.
No in-repo consumer other than Stats was located for the value on a follower, so no internal mechanism was found that misbehaves because of it.
unknowns: whether the omission is deliberate, i.e. whether the published commit index is intended to mean only the value the leader last advertised
whether any consumer outside the module relies on the value on a restarted node
whether the intended repair advances the commit index during the restore or derives the published value from the last snapshot index
question.trigger_rationale: NewRaft restores the newest snapshot that loads and restoreSnapshot then publishes raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot from the snapshot index and rebuilds the committed and latest configurations, but it never writes the commit index, which is otherwise written only in the appendEntries commit branch as min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex). A node that restarts from a snapshot therefore publishes zero for an index it reports as applied and as its last snapshot, and the same node had reported that index as committed before the restart. Within this prefix the restarted node's own last index is the snapshot index, so equal to J and not below J coincide and the comparison is unambiguous.

obligation.description: A node that reconstructs its state at startup from a stored snapshot through index J must publish a commit context at least J: the value Raft.CommitIndex() reports may not name a commit point below the snapshot state the node has itself restored and taken as applied.

scope.description: A node in the captured module constructed by NewRaft over stores that already hold a snapshot which the same node produced, observed before any election or leader contact.
assumptions: the stored snapshot is one the node itself took after committing and applying through its index
the restarted node's last index is the snapshot index, so no legal commit index exceeds it
excluded: the correctness of the snapshot payload itself, which the check does not inspect
the configuration carried by the snapshot
behaviour after an election or a leader contact has advanced the value
any requirement on callers or transports outside the module

pending: which consumers rely on the published value on a restarted node
whether the repair advances the commit index during the restore or derives the published value from the last snapshot index

grounding.derivation: Raft.CommitIndex() is documented as the committed index and as the basis for the read-index optimisation and returns raftState.commitIndex (s-api-commit-index). During construction NewRaft scans the log, restores the newest snapshot that loads, and restoreSnapshot publishes raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot from the snapshot index and rebuilds the committed and latest configurations without ever writing the commit index (s-api-restore-snapshot, s-api-newraft-config). The snapshot the node restores was taken by the same node after it had applied and committed through that index (s-snapshot-take), so the entries it covers are stored by a quorum of the configuration the snapshot carries. The obligation therefore requires the published commit index to be at least the restored snapshot index.
grounding.applicability: Applies to any node whose construction restores a stored snapshot. The check exercises a single node that took the snapshot itself and is then reconstructed over the same stores, with timers long enough that nothing else changes it before the read.
unresolved: whether the published value is intentionally limited to the leader's last advertised commit index, which no source states
whether any consumer depends on the value on a restarted node
alternatives: the zero could be read as 'no commit index has been advertised yet', but the node has itself restored and applied the committed state and reports that snapshot index in Stats

associations.rationale: This entry point is the located implementation of the publishing duty on the recovery path: it takes the snapshot's committed state as applied and stable, but leaves the index the node publishes as committed below it, and the same value is what the exported accessor and Stats report.

bindings.description: Raft.restoreSnapshot lists the stored snapshots, restores the newest one that loads, publishes raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot from the snapshot index and rebuilds the committed and latest configurations, but never writes the commit index, so a node constructed over a snapshot publishes a commit index below the state it has just restored.
pending: whether the commit index should be advanced here or derived from the last snapshot index
